evals.prompt:
/grill-me

I'm planning to add a new data source (Kaufland marketplace) to our data pipeline. It'll follow the same medallion architecture — bronze ingestion, silver cleaning, gold unification with existing Shopify/Amazon data, platinum enrichment. I'll create new Pandera schemas for each layer, new SRF configs, and plug it into the existing SageMaker orchestration. Should be straightforward since we already handle Amazon and Shopify.
evals.expected_output: A structured interview that identifies risks specific to adding a new marketplace: schema differences from existing sources, SRF naming conventions, gold-layer unification challenges (different field names/semantics across marketplaces), test fixture generation, and rollout strategy. Should explore the codebase first to understand existing patterns before asking questions.

evals.prompt:
/grill-me

We want to replace the current DuckDB-based query layer in voidsapi with direct PostgreSQL queries. The DuckDB federation adds complexity and we think going straight to Postgres will simplify the codebase. We'd update database.py, remove the DuckDB dependency, and rewrite the SQL queries.
evals.expected_output: Should probe why DuckDB was chosen in the first place (columnar analytics performance), identify which queries would degrade with pure row-store Postgres, ask about the migration path for existing deployments, question whether this has been benchmarked, and check if any queries rely on DuckDB-specific features. Should explore voidsapi/io/database.py to understand current usage before asking.

evals.prompt:
/grill-me

I'm going to add real-time stock sync via webhooks instead of the current batch polling approach. Shopify will push inventory_level webhooks to a new endpoint in voidsapi, and we'll update the database immediately instead of waiting for the next SageMaker pipeline run.
evals.expected_output: Should question: webhook reliability and retry handling, consistency between real-time updates and batch pipeline (which one is source of truth?), multi-tenant webhook routing, authentication/validation of incoming webhooks, what happens when webhook delivery fails, how this interacts with the existing alert calculation that assumes batch data, and whether the existing schema supports event-driven updates. Should explore both projects to understand current stock flow.
